extracted.intended_audience: joint force commanders, public affairs officers (PAOs), and public affairs planners involved in joint military operations
extracted.subtask_short: public affairs planning in joint ops
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative standards for planning, integrating, and executing public affairs (PA) activities across the joint operation planning process, including media operations, intelligence support, interagency coordination, and annex development.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA participation across JOPP
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin analysis of the operational environment; participate in JIPOE; provide PA perspective during mission analysis; participate in COA development, analysis/wargaming, comparison, and approval; provide PA input to plan or order development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify PA tasks (specified, implied, essential), intelligence requirements for PA, develop PA estimates, facts and assumptions, and participate in cross-functional staff organizations throughout the JOPP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annex F (Public Affairs) content
rubrics_metrics.description: Annex F of an OPORD should address all PA-related transportation, communications, billeting, equipment, and personnel resources required to support the plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture additional planning considerations (e.g., media access, visual information, embedding/media pools, AFRTS) in Annex F; Annex F complements but does not replace the PPAG forwarded to OASD(PA). A sample Annex F is provided in Appendix B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribute to Annex Y (Strategic Communication)
rubrics_metrics.description: PA planners will contribute to the development of Annex Y and use its content to inform Annex F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annex Y should include situation and CONOPS focusing on the information environment, opposition, lines of operation, measures of effectiveness, tasks, and coordination instructions (per CJCSM 3122.03C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed Public Affairs Guidance (PPAG) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: PPAG should include recommended PA policy, background, contingency statements, message points, answers to anticipated media questions, community engagement guidance, and details governing the release of information to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop PPAG in sufficient time for coordination; submit PPAG through CCDRs to OASD(PA) for approval; OASD(PA) will approve/modify/disapprove. Approved PAG should be published prior to deployment; supplemental PPAG may continue during operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of PAG publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Approved PAG should be published prior to the start of any deployment activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the very latest, PAG must be published in conjunction with receipt of an EXORD; development of additional/supplemental PPAG continues as needed throughout operation or campaign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis Action Planning augmentation
rubrics_metrics.description: In CAP, accelerated decisionmaking may require immediate augmentation of the PA staff to handle planning while responding to intense public and media interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure requisite personnel are available for planning while dealing with increased operational tempo; be prepared to develop/approve COA, publish orders, prepare forces, and arrange sustainment in days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synchronize PA across the joint force and agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: During initial planning it is critical to synchronize PA planning and activities across the joint force and with other agencies as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish authorities to plan, integrate, approve, and disseminate information and imagery; coordinate legal considerations (e.g., investigations, law of war violations) early in PAG; coordinate overall themes and media support prior to hostilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate Strategic Communication guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: PA planners should analyze SC guidance and ensure PA activities align with commanders' operational objectives and SC guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify intended audiences, themes, messages, actions, desired effects, and objectives during planning; synchronize PA, DSPD, IO, and other SC-related capabilities; ensure consistency with USG SC objectives and public diplomacy efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intelligence support to PA (JIPOE usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding the operational environment via JIPOE is fundamental; intelligence can identify influencers and provide imagery to support PA missions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA may request ISR platforms gather imagery for PA; PA may require access to relevant intelligence products to assist development of PA news releases; consider systems perspective to identify links and nodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media operations planning and embedding
rubrics_metrics.description: PA plans should include detailed processes/procedures to give media opportunities to meet personnel conducting operations, including embedding media with units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish specific ground rules for embedding that are thoroughly understood by media and unit; plan for accommodating/supporting media escorted by personnel not formally trained in PA; address commander security concerns in access decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media accompaniment of commanders
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders may have media accompany them on visits to operating units to provide perspective from senior leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This option benefits media who cannot embed long-term and offers access to leadership viewpoints; plan and coordinate accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local and regional media support and language capability
rubrics_metrics.description: PA should support local and regional media consistent with JFC instructions, including cultural and language capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News releases and public information Internet sites should have local/regional language capability; media facilitation, response, and escort operations must accommodate non-English-speaking reporters; media analysis must consider cultural context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely coverage planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans must assist the media in getting information out accurately and timely to compete in the information environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commit equipped/trained joint PA teams; determine lift/logistic support for PA and media personnel and products; hold frequent in-theater briefings; institute rapid dissemination processes for weapons systems video, ISR data, and COMCAM products; delegate release authority to the lowest possible level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual Information (VI) and Combat Camera (COMCAM) coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: PA planners work with VI/COMCAM supervisors to ensure PA requirements are identified and considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial multimedia products are copyrighted and cannot be used without consent; incorporate COMCAM requirements into plans and coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command information inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders should plan for inclusion of command information personnel in operations to assist leadership communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOD command information programs help commanders perform leadership communications functions and keep military elements informed.

rubrics_metrics.name: AFRTS deployment and use
rubrics_metrics.description: AFRTS deployment offers a means to communicate directly to DOD personnel in operational areas and other locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider radio service for bare-base/forward areas, TV for rear areas as operations mature; AFRTS can provide MOC video newsgathering capabilities and immediate announcements to DOD personnel when approved; AFRTS requires approvals for frequencies/real estate and cannot be used for political purposes or MISO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community engagement planning
rubrics_metrics.description: PA provides specialized skills to plan and develop relationships for commanders interacting within local communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Involve PA in planning/preparation/execution of local/HN engagements to support CMO; seek creative uses of community engagement capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense Support to Public Diplomacy (DSPD) coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: DSPD consists of DOD activities to support U.S. government public diplomacy and ensure coherent messaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure DOD information activities are in concert with broader USG communications strategy and National Security Strategy; DSPD requires interagency coordination among DOD components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate through Country Team and embassy channels
rubrics_metrics.description: PA staff should coordinate all themes, messages, and press releases impacting a host nation through the respective US embassy channels; the COM controls information release in country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish coordination via the PAO at the embassy and align with IO planners; country team unifies US policy implementation and advises the COM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency coordination for consistent messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: CCDRs operate with interagency partners whose actions can affect public understanding; communicating a consistent message that supports approved themes is essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agree early on procedures for media access, credentials, briefing, escorting, and transport; OASD(PA) interfaces with combatant commands and passes interagency guidance through PAG; Executive Office of the President leads SC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with IGOs and NGOs
rubrics_metrics.description: Close coordination with intergovernmental and non-governmental organizations helps ensure consistent information about the total US response effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When DOD provides FHA or works with many agencies, coordinate to avoid conflicting information and to reflect contributions of other parties accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host nation consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: PA planners should consult with host nation governments to identify local issues and concerns to be reflected in PAG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish coordination through embassy PAO and with IO planners as appropriate; respect host nation sensitivities when crafting messages and releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider multinational partner sensitivities
rubrics_metrics.description: PA planning should reflect the possibility of multinational partners and be cognizant of their concerns when communicating with media and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for partner sensitivities in messaging and MOC staff communications to avoid diplomatic friction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor PA to specific operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders should ensure PA activities are tailored across the range of military operations to provide background, rationale, and operation-specific elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to discuss structure, strategy, objectives, tactics, training, logistics, intelligence, and troop support; plan for differing media interest peaks depending on operation type.

rubrics_metrics.name: FHA-specific PA constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: FHA missions involve a balance of political and military objectives and often require intensive PA coordination with NGOs and other agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid preempting political authority or appearing to take credit for others' efforts; coordinate via CMOC or country team; expect increased PA capabilities will be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counterdrug operation sensitivities
rubrics_metrics.description: CD operations have legal and law enforcement sensitivities that generate additional concerns regarding release of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider effects on safety of personnel, pending judicial cases, and security of intelligence systems; closely coordinate with agency PA counterparts and include OPSEC measures in PA plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combating terrorism PA objectives and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Antiterrorism/CT environments are media-intense; PA must anticipate near-live coverage and balance public information needs against value to terrorists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure accurate information and communicate a calm, measured reaction; coordinate with OASD(PA) as single point of contact for PA aspects of CT operations; protect OPSEC, technology security, and INFOSEC.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEO PA approval and readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: For Noncombatant Evacuation Operations, PAO should plan and coordinate releases with embassy personnel and ensure COM or designated representative has approved all PA announcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs must be prepared to conduct media operations in any environment (including afloat) and coordinate rapidly due to the operation's speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peace operations information management
rubrics_metrics.description: In peace operations, parties may release slanted information; PA should reduce speculation by providing releasable information on a timely basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate orchestrated media operations by parties and proactively supply accurate, timely information to set the record straight.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMO/CA coordination to avoid conflicting information
rubrics_metrics.description: PA must coordinate with Civil-Military Operations and Civil Affairs to ensure information released does not conflict with other efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate primarily through the CMOC and regular staff channels to synchronize messaging and dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: CWMD and CBRN information coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: CWMD and CBRN missions require integrated interagency and multinational coordination; PA should work with USG agencies/NGOs to communicate risk and response information quickly and effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WMD information release may require non-DOD authorities (e.g., DOS); COMCAM can document WMD sites if tasked; follow JP guidance and classification guides where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain continuous dialogue with media and cultural attunement
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a need for continuous dialogue between the joint force and media; formulate and deliver timely and culturally attuned messages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess direct/indirect effects of actions on perceptions and should seek regular opportunities to work with the media; consider audiences in allied/partner nations and regional publics.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA liaison role and non-interference with reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: PA personnel should act as liaisons to help media understand events but should not interfere with the reporting process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The JFC or designated representative should conduct frequent operational briefings to inform audiences and respond to media questions while preserving independent reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media credentialing criteria and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for credentialing journalists are established by the joint force PAO or MOC director; credentialing validates individuals as journalists and ensures treatment under law of war if captured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credentialing is not intended to restrict access; encourage registration of non-credentialed journalists and request adherence to ground rules; suspension/expulsion of credentials requires concurrence of JFC and CCDR.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOC role and registration expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The MOC serves as a logistic and information base for media relations; journalists seeking credentials are asked to agree to ground rules tailored to the operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders should not provide information to non-credentialed journalists without guidance; non-credentialed journalists should be encouraged to register and abide by ground rules; participation in DOD-hosted training should not be a prerequisite for accompanying forces absent unusual circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media ground rules objectives and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Ground rules protect DOD members from release of information that could threaten security while facilitating media access to timely, relevant information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground rules reconcile media desire to cover operations with DOD security/safety and include processes for release of information, media access to the commander, internet access if not commercially available, and process for unintentional exposure to classified information.
